sentence.text: European steel is decarbonising by reducing iron ore with hydrogen instead of coke, and the main question is who pays for it.

why_it_matters.text: Steel made this way costs more than the steel it replaces, so whether Europe gets it depends on who covers the difference.

facts.label: The gap
facts.text: Low-carbon steel costs 50-140% above a conventional BF-BOF plant to make, on the International Energy Agency's figures.

facts.label: Pipeline
facts.text: 8 European steel projects are under way, and 7 of them have taken a final investment decision.

facts.label: Decisive exposure
facts.text: European steel makers are losing the free carbon allowances they used to get, worth €2.58 per tonne at today's carbon price.

facts.label: The latest
facts.text: greentec steel Linz went into construction on 18 June 2026.

facts.label: Binding constraint
facts.text: Green premium against willingness to pay — a market constraint, acted on by 6 ranked measures at 4.5 of combined weight.
